Indrajit's Illusory Sita

Stories from the Ramayana

Indrajit's Illusory Sita

A conjuring made to break Rama

In everyday English — Yuddha Kanda, sargas 81–84

Stories by Eku

How to Read · · BEFORE WE BEGIN

Read it out loud. This story is made to be told. Read slowly, as if you are sitting with everyone at home.

This book is a story of trickery — what you see is not what is true. Where there is illusion, read slowly and gravely; where the truth opens, let light into your voice.

The yellow boxes hold the characters' own words. Change your voice a little as you speak them — Indrajit threatening, Hanuman frightened, Vibhishana calm.

(Purple hints) tell you where to pause, whisper, or raise your voice. They are for the reader — do not read them aloud.

The green box at the end of each part — Pause and think. Stop there. Ask questions. Let the listeners speak.

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 81–84 — Indrajit's illusory Sita. The part that tells of the conjured killing carries the ◆ mark at the top. No killing, blood, or death is shown in any picture — only the moment before it. Anything more you may want to know is given separately at the end, in Where This Story Comes From.

Who's Who · · WHO'S WHO

Rama — prince of Ayodhya, bearer of the bow. Warm dark-brown skin, a calm and kind face, fully clothed, barefoot in the forest. In this book he breaks with grief.

Lakshmana — Rama's younger brother, slightly lighter in complexion, bow in hand. He comforts Rama.

Indrajit — son of Ravana, also called Meghanada. Master of illusion, performing a rite at Nikumbhila.

Hanuman — son of the Wind, minister of Sugriva, messenger of Rama. Light golden-brown fur, long tail, gentle devoted face, saffron dhoti. He sees the illusory Sita with his own eyes.

Vibhishana — Ravana's younger brother, who came to Rama's side for the sake of dharma. Calm and wise. He alone opens the secret of the illusion.

Sugriva — king of the vanaras, friend of Rama.

Sita — held captive in the Ashoka grove. Wheat-gold skin, long black braid with white jasmine flowers, small gold jhumka earrings, a thin gold nose-ring on her left nostril, a single pale saree, no crown. In this book she herself does not come — only her image comes.

Trijata — the elderly rakshasi who looks after Sita, kind and understanding.

1 · Indrajit's New Plan · · INDRAJIT'S NEW PLAN

Ravana's sons and generals had fallen one by one. Now only his greatest son remained — Indrajit.

Indrajit thought — “Rama is hard to defeat in battle. But if I break his heart — his bow will fall too.”

He needed time — time to complete the rite at Nikumbhila. If that rite were completed — he would become unbeatable. But the rite needed time — and to gain time he had to stop Rama.

Riding on his chariot, Indrajit announced — “Vanaras! Look! I will kill Sita before your very eyes — the one for whose sake you have all come here!”

The vanara army stood stunned. Hanuman stepped forward — and saw — a woman seated on Indrajit's chariot — just like Sita!

Pause and think — Indrajit does not want to fight Rama — he wants to break Rama's heart. Is breaking a heart more dangerous than defeating a body? And using trickery to gain time — is that also a weapon of war?

2 · The Living Image · · THE LIVING IMAGE

◆ ◆ This part is not for younger listeners — it tells of a frightening conjuring. Elders, please read it gently.

The woman seated on the chariot looked just like Sita. The same pale saree, the same long braid, the same jasmine flowers, the same gold nose-ring. She seemed alive — breathing, frightened.

Seeing her, the vanaras cried out — “Sita! He has brought Sita!” Even Hanuman stood stunned — could Sita truly be here?

Indrajit said — “Look — now I will kill her — and then all of you, Rama, Lakshmana, Sugriva and Vibhishana too.”

And he did it — before everyone's eyes. Cries of horror rose from the vanara army. The tree slipped from Hanuman's hands.

(Pause here — stay silent for a few moments. Do not tell this part in detail.)

Pause and think — What was seen — was not true. But how were the vanaras to know? Can eyes sometimes lie? And when something happens before your very eyes — can it still not be true?

3 · Hanuman Runs with the News · · HANUMAN RUNS WITH THE NEWS

What Hanuman had seen — he had to tell Rama. He ran — toward Rama's camp. The vanara army ran behind him — one fear in every heart.

Hanuman reached Rama — panting, tears in his eyes.

Hanuman said — “Rama! Indrajit has killed Sita — before everyone's eyes!”

When Rama heard this — his bow slipped from his hand. He sank to the earth — as if all his strength had been taken from him.

Lakshmana came running — “Brother!” — but Rama could not speak.

Pause and think — Hanuman told what he had seen, believing it true. Is it wrong to tell what you saw — or right? And Rama's bow slipping from his hand — is that defeat — or grief?

4 · Rama Breaks · · RAMA BREAKS

Rama sat on the earth — drowned in grief. One thought filled his mind — Sita is gone. The one for whom he had come to Lanka — she is no more.

He thought — “I have lost Sita. Now what is the war for? Now what is life for?”

Rama said — “Lakshmana, now all is in vain. Without Sita, Ayodhya too is in vain, the war too is in vain.”

The vanara army was silent. No roaring, no drums. The whole army — which had been fighting until now — was drowned in grief.

(Read this part very slowly — as if someone is weeping.)

Pause and think — Rama — who had stood unmoved until now — has broken. Can even the greatest warrior break? And is breaking a weakness — or a sign of love?

5 · Lakshmana's Words · · LAKSHMANA'S WORDS

Lakshmana sat beside Rama — and took his hand.

Lakshmana said — “Brother, rise! Grief will achieve nothing. It is for Sita that we came here — and for Sita that we must fight.”

“If you yourself break — what will become of the army? Of Sugriva? Of Hanuman? Rise, brother — take up your bow!”

Rama looked at Lakshmana — but could not rise. His heart was still with Sita.

Lakshmana said again — “Brother, what happened — happened in war. But the war is not yet over. Ravana still lives — and Sita's vengeance is still owed.”

Rama closed his eyes. He wanted to rise — but grief would not let him rise.

Pause and think — Lakshmana told Rama to rise — but Rama could not. Is a younger brother advising an elder brother also a kind of duty? And when someone wants to rise — but cannot — what should they do?

6 · Vibhishana Arrives · · VIBHISHANA ARRIVES

Then Vibhishana came — calm, unhurried. He saw — Rama sitting on the earth, Lakshmana beside him, the army silent.

Vibhishana asked — “Rama, what has happened? Why do you sit like this?”

Hanuman told him — “Indrajit has killed Sita — before everyone's eyes.”

When Vibhishana heard this — he was silent for a moment. Then a faint understanding came to his face — as if a riddle had been solved.

Vibhishana said — “Rama, hear me — first learn what is true and what is illusion.”

Pause and think — Vibhishana did not believe the news at once — he paused for a moment. Is pausing on hearing news also wisdom? And when everyone is weeping — is it not hard to stay calm?

7 · It Was a Conjuring · · IT WAS A CONJURING

Vibhishana said — “Rama, what you heard — is not true. Sita is alive — she sits in the Ashoka grove, under Trijata's care.”

Vibhishana said — “Indrajit made an image of Sita by illusion — like a living one. That was an image — not Sita. He killed it before your eyes — so that you would break — and he could gain time.”

Rama opened his eyes — “Time? Time for what?”

Vibhishana said — “For the rite at Nikumbhila. Indrajit is performing a rite there — and if that rite is completed — he will become unbeatable. That is why he made this illusion — so that you would stay drowned in grief — and he could complete his rite.”

The darkness lifted from Rama's mind. Sita is alive! Knowing this, his strength began to return.

(Let light into your voice here — as if morning is coming.)

Pause and think — What died — was not Sita — only her image. Is killing an image also murder — or trickery? And how did Vibhishana know — did he know Indrajit — or did he recognise illusion?

8 · To Nikumbhila · · TO NIKUMBHILA

Rama rose to his feet. He took up his bow — and looked at Lakshmana.

Vibhishana said — “Do not delay now. Indrajit's rite must be stopped before it is completed. Lakshmana — you go — with Hanuman and the vanaras — to Nikumbhila!”

Lakshmana took up his bow. Hanuman took up his mace. The vanara army began to roar again — grief had now turned to anger.

Rama said — “Go, Lakshmana. Stop Indrajit — before his rite is complete.”

But the battle of Nikumbhila — that story is the next book's.

Pause and think — Rama had broken — and then he rose again. Is knowing the truth itself the strength to rise? And Lakshmana marches to Nikumbhila — has this war now become only between Indrajit and Lakshmana?

Where This Story Comes From · · WHERE THIS STORY COMES FROM

Main source

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 81–84 — Indrajit's illusory Sita.

Indrajit's new plan — sarga 81

Indrajit announcing before the army that he will kill Sita before everyone's eyes — and conjuring a living image of Sita by illusion — this is in sarga 81.

The living image — sarga 81

The illusory Sita looking as if alive; Indrajit killing her before everyone's eyes; the horror of the vanara army — this is in sarga 81. In this book the killing is told only in words, briefly — the pictures do not show that moment.

Hanuman's news — sarga 82

Hanuman running to Rama and bringing him the news of Sita's death — this is in sarga 82.

Rama's grief — sarga 83

Rama breaking down with grief; Lakshmana comforting him and urging him to rise — this is in sarga 83.

Vibhishana opens the secret — sarga 84

Vibhishana arriving; explaining that the real Sita is alive in the Ashoka grove under Trijata's care; the illusory Sita was only an image; Indrajit made this trick to gain time for the rite at Nikumbhila — this is in sarga 84.

The rite at Nikumbhila

The rite Indrajit is performing at Nikumbhila — once it is completed, he will become unbeatable. That is why Vibhishana says it must be stopped before it is completed. The battle to stop the rite is the next book's story.

About the pictures

This book's pictures never show a killing, blood, or death. The picture of the illusory Sita shows only the moment before — the image standing, and Indrajit standing beside her. In the last pictures the truth opens — Sita sits alive in the Ashoka grove.

What happens next

Lakshmana, Hanuman and the vanaras are marching to Nikumbhila — to stop Indrajit's rite. That battle is the next book of this series.
